title: Great memories
summary: How a simple scene led me to amazing life wisdom.
content:
When you get a wonderful meaning, or let's say when you finally understand it, it's a great memory. In that moment, we get an extra life, as wisdom increases our life; in different words, it increases the value and quality of our life. In this regard, I will tell you what this lovely tree taught me.

I saw the sky twice in the same place and under the same trees. The first time, the sky was obscured from me by the branches of the trees. It was difficult to see the beautiful horizon. At that time, a person might feel as if they were in a prison. How would a person live if the sky was obscured from them? What is our feeling toward these branches that prevent us from seeing the sky and the birds? Is it possible to see their beauty or some of the positive aspects that every creature carries? But wait a moment... before continuing with these bitter questions, here the tree opens a gate to heaven for us! And at that moment, I felt that the universe welcomed me. The clouds, birds, and tree branches were clapping for me with the sounds of their laughter carried by the breeze.

Then I discovered that those branches in the first picture were not a prison or something that calls for frustration or anger. On the contrary, they are the obstacles that we face in life and because of them, we become better versions of ourselves. The difficult situations that happen to us not only teach us and give us wisdom, but also give us a more beautiful life. Because life is awareness, and when we are in a state of awareness, we are really alive, meaning that we are actually living! Therefore, when I saw the sky in the second image, it was indescribably amazing and joyful, because the first image made me think and meditate. After I became closer to realization, I became ready for awareness and tasted an amazing sense of life.

title: Reflections on the Meaning of (Islam)
summary: Why the word Islam was chosen, and how it reflects absolute submission and faith in the unseen.
content:
Islam (إسلام) is an Arabic word meaning absolute submission. Given that in Arabic it is rare for synonyms to be exact synonyms, meaning that they may reflect the same meaning, but each synonym has a deeper, broader, or more precise degree in a particular direction, the word Islam is considered a synonym of submission, but it is deeper in that it points to the utmost degree of submission, which we call absolute submission.

There are many reflections and analyses of the indications of the meaning of the word Islam that reflect the essence of the religion of Islam in terms of absolute submission to God. But some questions may wander in the mind: given that the religion of Islam is a monotheistic religion above all, focusing on and emphasizing the One God, who has no partner and no equal, why does it not carry a name essentially linked to the attribute of monotheism?

There are many possible and convincing answers, in that a person submits to God through voluntary humility by worshipping the One God, believing in Him, following His guidance, and unconditionally acknowledging His beautiful names and attributes.

There is also the spiritual and invisible side that the Holy Quran calls (the world of the unseen). It is the world that is not physically tangible in the current stage of human life on Earth, and belief in it requires submission to God Almighty, in that you do not see the angels but you believe with certainty in their existence.

But what if the matter carries other considerations alongside the previous answers? What if absolute submission to God Almighty is the only solution to the limitations of reason and perception on one hand, and to illusions on the other? To clarify what I mean: what can a human being imagine of an infinite universe? Here we are talking about real and tangible matters that do not fall within the world of the unseen: the expansion and endlessness of the universe, and the limits of our perception, in that when we speak of the universe we always mean (the observable universe, the part we have been able to observe). In this context, there is a large gap between what we have in our minds and perception and the truth of the universe in which we live. It is difficult for many earthly beings to grasp the meaning of immortality and eternity, and the inevitability of (the circle and cycle) seems to be something the mind finds hard to escape.

What is said here may seem to be nothing more than a detailed analysis of the meaning of belief in the unseen, for belief in the unseen requires leaving the earthly cage, not only in body but also in thought and mind. Here again we realize that our minds are designed in a particular direction at present, in a way that ensures we continue seriously doing what we must do for life on Earth, without the fact of inevitable death for every being becoming a barrier or obstacle to that, which in itself is extremely strange and part of the miracle itself. In the normal case, if you realized that you might suddenly disappear, along with everything around you, and you do not know exactly when, this might be an incentive to stop living; but what happens in the normal earthly condition is the opposite. From this perspective we clearly see a large gap between reality and truth, and we also notice that it is governed by our experiences on one hand, by the design of our way of thinking, and by the level of perception or consciousness present in our souls or somewhere within us, which is itself a physically unknown place. For the mind, the heart, and the brain, if you dissect them, you will not find in them anything of the ideas, convictions, principles, and judgments that give your life meaning. The soul is invisible, belongs to the world of the unseen, and is a guest here. The last sentence may be an answer to the earthly challenges of distinguishing between what is reality and what is truth, and thus reaching the point of submission to God and belief in the world of the unseen, which tells us about a small part of it. For God Almighty has said in the Holy Quran: “And you have not been given of knowledge except a little.” And God has described those who reject faith as being connected to the limited knowledge they have, which cannot take them beyond the point they insist on.

But insisting on the limits of knowledge is not the same as dismissing the intellect. On the contrary, we notice in the Holy Quran that the intellect is a direct path to faith: it questions inherited beliefs and weighs them against logic and evidence. Yet the intellect has a limit, and it knows its limit. Imam al Ghazali captured this simply: the intellect helps the sick reach the doctor, but once there, it leaves the treatment to the doctor. So too, the intellect leads you to God; and when you reach Him, its role ends. What lies beyond that point is not an abandonment of the intellect, but an acknowledgment of where it ends.

Accordingly, perhaps the main challenge of belief in the unseen, which is the essence of faith, does not lie in obedience and compliance, even though these are an essential part of it, but the challenge lies in heading toward a path that your mind finds hard to grasp. Here the wisdom of God’s name, the All-Merciful, the Ever-Merciful becomes clear, the most frequently mentioned of the beautiful names in the Holy Quran, especially since the Holy Quran begins with these names, and they are recited again before every surah of the Quran. Accordingly, a person can find reassurance and spiritual peace through only one means: absolute submission to God in everything. And because God, the All-Merciful, the Ever-Merciful, is the Wise, the Knower of the unseen and the seen, and is aware of our weakness and the limits of our consciousness compared with what we do not know and cannot fully perceive with our current earthly identities, He has chosen for us absolute submission to Him, to His beautiful names, and to His lofty attributes.
